name: Manage derivative overlays, currency hedges and leverage
summary: The total portfolio team uses equity and bond futures, currency forwards and swaps to rebalance client portfolios quickly, hedge foreign currency to each client's policy, run active asset allocation and dynamic currency positions and, from 2022, apply leverage at the total portfolio level. For each adjustment an analyst sizes the trades by client account, risk checks counterparty limits, policy ranges and leverage, the cash team checks margin capacity, larger changes go to the head of total portfolio management, and orders are keyed, released and sent to the trading desk, then verified after execution. Rolling contracts and keeping hedges in line with changing client weights make this steady daily work; stale exposure data, multiple checks run in sequence and margin needs in volatile markets are the main sources of delay and risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Five client portfolios with different hedge policies and asset mixes; overlays sit in client accounts and the money market and other line. Leverage of about $2.7 billion was applied at the total portfolio level by the end of 2022. Trade execution, confirmation and margin calls are separate processes.

trigger: An approved rebalancing proposal needs futures or currency changes, a liquidity report calls for freeing cash or margin, or the daily check shows a hedge ratio out of tolerance or a contract due to roll.
end_state: The adjustment has been executed, verified against target exposures, notified to the cash team and logged, or it was netted away or deferred.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at quarterly futures and forward roll dates, month-end rebalancing and in volatile markets; leverage added from 2022 raised volumes.

steps.name: Receive the overlay request or daily trigger
steps.description: A total portfolio manager picks up the reason for an overlay change: an approved rebalancing proposal asking for futures or currency changes, a liquidity report action to free cash or margin, or the morning overlay check showing a client's currency hedge ratio outside tolerance or a futures or forward contract due to roll.

error.defect_description: A request is read with the wrong client or direction.

evidence.note: Overlays for rebalancing, dynamic foreign exchange and active asset allocation (from 2020) and total portfolio leverage (from 2022) are described; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Pull exposures, positions and cash
steps.description: A total portfolio analyst pulls the affected client accounts' futures and forward positions, foreign currency exposure including a look-through of pool holdings, cash and margin balances, and current prices and exchange rates.

error.defect_description: An exposure is stale or incomplete, such as a pool look-through lag or private assets' currency taken from last quarter.

evidence.note: Data sources follow the organisation file's systems; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Net requests across clients and decide whether to trade
steps.description: The portfolio manager nets the request against other clients' requests and against expected cash flows, which can cancel the need to trade, and decides whether to go ahead, or to defer when the trade needs an instrument or counterparty that is not yet approved.

evidence.note: Using flows to rebalance reduces transaction costs; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Size the adjustment for each client account
steps.description: The analyst calculates, in the overlay workbook, the number of equity index or bond futures contracts, or the notional of currency forwards or swaps, needed to reach each client's target exposure, hedge ratio or leverage, choosing contract month or forward tenor and the roll date.

error.defect_description: Wrong contract multiplier, sign, currency or hedge base.

evidence.note: Futures and forwards adjust exposure without trading physical assets; currency forwards are short-dated and rolled. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Portfolio manager checks the sizing
steps.description: The portfolio manager checks the sized trades against the request and the client's targets, looking for sign errors and unreasonable sizes, and picks the instrument route.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check counterparty limits and documentation
steps.description: For currency forwards and swaps, a manager in investment risk oversight checks that the chosen banks are approved, that the client account has signed ISDA and collateral agreements with them, and that exposure stays within each counterparty's credit limit after netting.

control.basis: Counterparty credit limits and ISDA netting requirements in the investment risk framework

evidence.note: Counterparty exposure is measured on notional, current and potential future exposure, netted under ISDA agreements and monitored daily against limits; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check policy ranges, risk and leverage
steps.description: A risk analyst runs the post-trade exposures through the risk system: each client's asset mix ranges and restrictions, active risk and, from 2022, the client's leverage target and the pool-level leverage limits.

control.basis: Client investment policy ranges and the model manager leverage framework and guideline (2022)

evidence.note: Leverage framework with client targets and pool limits, and client leverage targets, are stated; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check margin and collateral capacity
steps.description: The cash and collateral analyst checks that each client account has the cash or treasury bills for initial margin on new futures, a buffer for daily variation margin and eligible collateral for forwards, and flags accounts where liquidity is tight.

error.defect_description: Margin need is underestimated for a volatile contract.

evidence.note: Futures are margined in cash daily; variation margin on uncleared derivatives is called daily and paid within two business days. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Head of total portfolio management approves
steps.description: Adjustments above the portfolio manager's authority, those that change a client's leverage or use a new type of instrument, need the managing director's approval; routine rolls and small hedge resets do not.

control.basis: Delegated authorities within the Total Portfolio Investment Department Committee framework

evidence.note: Investment Department Committees, including one for total portfolio, approve up to thresholds; the share needing approval is an author estimate.

steps.name: Enter orders in the order management system
steps.description: The analyst keys the orders by client account, or as a block with an allocation, with instrument, contract month or value date, quantity or notional and instructions such as a limit or a benchmark fixing time.

error.defect_description: Wrong account, side or value date keyed.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check and release the orders
steps.description: The portfolio manager compares each staged order with the approved sizing and releases it to the trading desk, or sends it back for correction.

control.basis: Four-eyes control: orders keyed by one person and released by another

evidence.note: Trades must be properly authorised and allocated by approved methods; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Automated pre-trade compliance check
steps.description: The order management system checks each order against the client's investment guidelines, permitted instruments, restricted lists and counterparty eligibility, and blocks or flags any breach.

control.basis: OSC exemption order on the model manager: compliance system prevents investments that contravene restrictions in each investment management agreement

evidence.note: Prevention of contraventions is required by the order; alert rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Compliance reviews the alert
steps.description: A compliance analyst reviews the flagged order, clears a false alert caused by stale data or a coding gap, or confirms a true breach and sends the order back to be resized.

control.basis: OSC exemption order on the model manager: compliance system and investment restrictions

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Trader accepts the order and plans execution
steps.description: A trader picks up the order, checks contract liquidity, the roll spread or forward points and the time of day, and chooses how to execute: a broker algorithm or calendar spread for futures, or competitive quotes or a benchmark fixing for currency forwards.

evidence.note: Execution itself belongs to the trade execution process; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Trading desk executes and reports fills
steps.description: The desk executes the order with brokers or dealer platforms and reports fills, prices and allocations back to the total portfolio team through the order management system.

error.defect_description: A fill is allocated to the wrong client account.

control.basis: Best execution policy (competitive quotes for currency forwards)

evidence.note: Author estimate; large orders may be worked over a day or more.

steps.name: Verify fills and post-trade exposures
steps.description: The analyst compares fills with intended quantities and prices, recalculates each client's exposure, hedge ratio and leverage, and sends any residual from partial fills or market moves back for a top-up.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Tell the cash team about margin and settlement needs
steps.description: The analyst sends the cash and collateral team the expected initial margin, the value dates and amounts of currency forward settlements and any collateral moves, so funding and the liquidity forecast are updated.

error.defect_description: A forward settlement date is not passed on.

evidence.note: Currency hedging settlements are an outflow in the liquidity coverage ratio; collateral is due within one or two days. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Record the adjustment in the overlay log
steps.description: The analyst records the reason, sizes by client, costs, approvals and resulting exposures in the overlay log used for monthly client reporting, attribution of active asset allocation and dynamic currency results, and audit.

control.basis: Trade records and authorisation evidence kept for the SOC 1 control environment

evidence.note: Active asset allocation and dynamic foreign exchange results are reported in the money market and other line; the model manager obtained a SOC 1 report. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Defer the trade pending counterparty or instrument approval
steps.description: When the trade needs a counterparty, clearing broker or instrument not yet approved for the client account, the portfolio manager defers it, starts the onboarding request and uses an approved alternative if one exists.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Netted away
exceptions.description: Requests from different clients or expected cash flows offset each other, so no trade is needed.

exceptions.name: Sizing or limit failure
exceptions.description: The sizing check, counterparty limit, risk range, margin capacity or head of total portfolio management sends the trade back to be resized.

exceptions.name: Compliance alert
exceptions.description: Pre-trade compliance flags an order; most are false alerts, a few are true breaches that need resizing.

exceptions.name: Residual after execution
exceptions.description: Partial fills or market moves leave exposure off target and a top-up is sized.

exceptions.name: Counterparty or instrument not approved
exceptions.description: The trade needs a new counterparty, clearing broker or instrument and is deferred until onboarding completes.

pain_points.description: Exposure data is often stale or incomplete (pool look-through lags, quarter-old private values), so sizing errors and post-trade top-ups are common.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the step structure.

pain_points.description: Counterparty, risk, margin and approval checks run one after another, each with its own queue, which can push a same-day adjustment to the next day.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the step structure.

pain_points.description: Futures margin and currency forward settlements can demand cash within a day or two when markets move sharply, which ties overlays to the liquidity forecast.

evidence.note: Margin is due within one or two days; regulators ask funds to prepare for margin calls; large liquidity demands in March 2020.

assumptions: Unit of work is one overlay adjustment across the affected client accounts; daily hedge-ratio resets and contract rolls are counted with the rebalancing trigger because they maintain overlay positions set through rebalancing proposals, as the process map lists only rebalancing and liquidity as triggers.
Market data from data vendors and client investment policies (hedge ratios, leverage targets) are listed as standing inputs; neither is on the process_map entry.
risk_analyst, investment_risk_manager, cash_collateral_analyst and compliance_analyst are organisation file roles not listed on this process_map entry; they perform the pre-trade checks.
Trading execution, confirmation, settlement and daily margin calls are separate processes; the trader's steps here cover only accepting the order and reporting fills.
The model manager has not published its overlay authorities, hedge tolerances or check sequence; shares and times are author estimates.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges.

sources.title: Guideline: Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives (2020)
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
sources.supports: Variation margin called daily with a minimum transfer amount of at most $750,000 and exchanged within two business days; initial margin phased in from September 2021 and September 2022; physically settled FX forwards and swaps excluded from margin requirements but counted toward thresholds.

sources.title: Dutch pension funds can meet margin calls on derivatives, but depend on functioning money markets
sources.supports: Pension funds must post collateral within one or two days of a derivative losing value; they draw on cash, repo and money market funds; stress tests used sharp interest rate and currency shocks.

sources.title: Liquidity Preparedness for Margin and Collateral Calls: Final report
sources.supports: Non-bank participants should include margin and collateral calls in liquidity risk management, stress test them under extreme but plausible conditions, hold sufficient liquid assets and keep collateral processes resilient; cites March 2020 and the September 2022 LDI fund episode.

sources.title: The rule for rebalancing the equity share in the Government Pension Fund Global
sources.supports: Large rebalancing trades are spread over time and use fund inflows to cut transaction costs; band-based triggers.

sources.title: Overlay program with an OCIO (insight article)
sources.supports: Futures overlays keep allocations on target without selling physical assets, useful with illiquid assets; swaps for precise hedges; collateral pools back overlay exposure.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.supports: Baseline control objective: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded in line with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; block orders allocated by approved methods. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.
